children: US soybean futures dipped on Friday but were headed for a weekly gain with Chinese demand in focus ahead of next week's meeting between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping and support from stronger soymeal prices.
on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) slipped 0.25% to $13.16-1/2 a bushel by 0106 GMT, but was up 1.54% for the week.
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday he planned to meet his Chinese counterpart this weekend.
US Midwest soymeal supplies have tightened in recent weeks as soybean processors extended seasonal maintenance shutdowns, limiting soymeal and soyoil output, brokers said.
eased 0.34% to $7.24-1/2 a bushel and was down 0.1% for the week as traders assessed shipment risks in the Black Sea region.

Wheat traders said an AFP report, which cited a Turkish proposal sent to Russia and Ukraine for a truce on strikes against commercial shipping in the Black Sea, put attention back on de-escalation prospects.

However, traders were cautious given that Turkey has already flagged such proposals, while a deal to halt strikes on energy infrastructure announced by U.S. President Trump on Monday had little effect on the ground.
BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, said in a note they expect ongoing export disruptions across Russia and Ukraine to keep underpinning wheat and corn prices through the
"We see little prospect of a near-term normalisation in Black Sea export volumes, and any market expectation of an imminent settlement is likely misguided," BMI said.

The International Grains Council raised its 2026/27 global wheat crop forecast by 3 million tons to 820 million, citing larger crops in Australia and Ukraine, but said trade flows remained slow amid Black Sea export disruptions.
It cut its global corn production forecast by 4 million tons to 1.301 billion.
rose 0.14% to $5.31-1/4 a bushel and was up 0.19% for the week.
Rains in parts of the upper Midwest have slowed corn harvesting, analysts said.
